title: Introduce weighted noise-sieve and ensemble canary evaluator to reduce false positives
author: Asha Menon
description: Motivation: We see recurring noisy alerts from the canary pipeline driven by transient traffic skews and heteroskedastic latency noise. This PR introduces two complementary mitigations: (1) a lightweight weighted noise-sieve that downweights high-variance slices when computing canary score, and (2) an ensemble canary evaluator that fuses multiple signal families (percentiles, throughput delta, tail-cohort drift) with calibrated voting. Goals: reduce false positives while preserving sensitivity to sustained regressions; keep runtime overhead small for the streaming canary path. What changed (high level): added a NoiseSieve module that computes slice-level variance and returns per-slice weights, implemented an EnsembleEvaluator that ingests existing probes and applies a learnable voting weight table, added an online calibration step that periodically fits weight damping on baseline windows, and extended the canary API to accept an explicit "sieve_profile" and "ensemble_profile" in the evaluation request. Implementation notes: the noise-sieve uses a robust estimator (median absolute deviation) to estimate per-slice dispersion; weights are clipped to [0.1,1.0] to avoid outright ignoring any slice; the ensemble uses a logistic blending of z-scored signals with a temperature hyperparameter exposed in the profile; online calibration runs every 6 hours by default and is bounded to <=10ms added p99 latency for evaluation. Testing and metrics: synthetic replay tests show a 37% reduction in false positives on historical noisy drift scenarios and a 14% improvement in regression detection precision for sustained 3-5% p95 shifts; e2e canary runs on canary-lab show CPU +4% and memory +2% for the pipeline component (within budget). Backwards compatibility: default behavior unchanged when no profile is provided; the sieve and ensemble are opt-in via profile in existing rollout configs. Rollout plan: land behind feature flag, run half of all internal canaries for 2 weeks, monitor aggregated FP rate and detection latency; if FP falls and detection latency is unchanged, unflag. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for NoiseSieve edge cases (constant slices, small-sample) ; - [x] Integration tests for EnsembleEvaluator fusion semantics ; - [x] Load test and perf budget verification ; - [x] Docs updated with new canary profiles spec ; - [x] Feature flag gating and rollout playbook added to runbook. Related: ENG-9876 outlines the baseline noise problem; SUP-4312 links to an incident where transient traffic bursts caused noisy alerts. Notes for reviewers: focus on the online calibration bounds, the clipping strategy for weights, and whether the ensemble voting table should be persisted as part of the canary run metadata. Migration: no data migration required. Merge method: squash and merge.

release_notes: Added a weighted noise-sieve and ensemble evaluator to reduce false positives in canary detection. Opt-in profiles available; default behavior unchanged. Improvements: lower FP rate in noisy traffic, configurable fusion weights and online calibration.
notes_for_ops: Feature gated. To enable for a workspace: add sieve_profile: 'default-weighted' and ensemble_profile: 'v1' to canary config. Monitor metrics: canary.false_positive_rate, canary.detection_latency_p95, canary.sieve_weight_skew. If unexpected regressions occur, flip feature flag and open incident channel #canary-ops.

hotfix: small patch to lower default online calibration frequency if perf budget breached
